newsitem.title: FRANCE: MEPs welcome more competition in rail services.
newsitem.headline: MEPs welcome more competition in rail services.

text.p: A proposal to increase competition in the provision of services for the European Union's railways got the green light from the European Parliament on Friday.
The European Commission has proposed updating a 1991 directive on the railways in order to speed up the introduction of competition -- COM(95)337.
MEPs approved the move but expressed concern that most member states had still not transposed vital elements of the 1991 directive into national law.

German Socialist Erich Farthofer said in his report on the proposal said there was unfair competition between incumbents and new entrants into the market because "the financial situation of public railway undertakings has been fully redressed in only one member state".
